questions.q: What does the 'Address Name' field actually represent when creating a supplier address?
options: The street address itself
An internal label you choose to identify the address, separate from the actual street/city/state/postal code
The supplier's legal entity name
The certifying agency
questions.explain: Address Name is a chosen identifier, while the physical address is entered in separate fields.

questions.q: What is a 'remit-to' purpose flag on a supplier address used for?
options: Marking the address where RFQs should be sent
Marking the address as the supplier's headquarters
Marking the address where payments or remittance advice should be sent
Marking the address as expired
questions.explain: A remit-to address is where payment or remittance advice is directed, which can differ from an ordering address.

questions.q: What distinguishes a business classification from a self-reported checkbox?
options: Nothing — it is purely self-reported
It can only be entered by Oracle support
It automatically changes the supplier's payment terms
It is meant to reflect a real certificate, with a certificate number, a certifying agency, and an expiration date
questions.explain: Classifications carry verifiable certification details rather than being an informal self-declaration.

questions.q: What happens when a supplier's business classification certificate is about to expire?
options: The system raises an alert, commonly within a 30-day window around the expiration date
The supplier is automatically deactivated
The classification is silently removed with no notice
All of the supplier's invoices are placed on hold
questions.explain: The system flags expired or soon-to-expire certifications so the business can act before compliance reporting is affected.

questions.q: Why does an expired business classification certificate matter operationally, even if purchasing from the supplier hasn't changed?
options: It has no real effect on anything
It automatically triggers a supplier merge
It can cause that supplier's spend to stop counting toward diversity or compliance reporting goals
It changes the supplier's tax registration number
questions.explain: An expired certificate can mean the spend no longer qualifies for diversity or compliance reporting, even though the purchasing itself is unchanged.
